target: 不过，也不好朝他们发火。教练太疼这些孩子了，也许溺爱过头，但不管怎样……

source: I like where things are going between us. His positivity is a good influence on me, I think. I've certainly been easing up on the blood pressure medication.
target: 我挺喜欢，我们现在这进展。他的积极，对我影响不错。血压药，确实都吃少了。

source: I suppose I'll play along. I don't want to seem cheap and unsupportive.
target: 那就配合一下。我可不想显得，小气又不支持。

source: Making a good impression is so important in these early stages. I'm sure Coach is overthinking his response too...
target: 刚开始，留下好印象，多重要。教练肯定，也在纠结怎么回应……

source: Hmmm... oh, God, did I leave the oven on?!
target: 嗯……天啊，烤箱是不是忘关了？！

source: I'm back. Very well, I'll donate a bit of money to your "charity."
target: 回来了。好吧，给你们的“慈善”，捐点钱。

source: It's good for young folk to be involved in nature conservationist efforts. Wouldn't you agree, Coach?
target: 年轻人参与自然保护，是好事。教练，你说呢？

source: Yeah. Sure. Give 'em +N3 MONEY for all I care. I need to check on my apartment right now immediately.
target: 嗯，行。给他们+N3金钱吧，随便。我得现在、立刻，回公寓检查！

source: Nice, free money! You lose -N6 SOUL for the underhanded way you acquired it, but you gain +N3 HYPE for pulling off your prank!
target: 漂亮，白来的钱！手段不光彩，让你损失-N6灵魂。不过，恶作剧成功，你获得+N3热度！

source: Feet aficionado gathering
target: 足部爱好者聚会

source: You roll up to the 31st Annual Afeetcionado Gathering. That's what it says on the commemorative socks you get at the entrance, anyway.
target: 你来到第三十一届年度足迷大会。至少，门口发的纪念袜子上，是这么写的。

source: Well gang, we're not in Kansas anymore. Let's mingle!
target: 各位，这下算进了新世界。交际去！

source: Hello there, sir! I'm guessing you've got some wacky-ass, kinky opinions on the Desert Foot?
target: 您好，先生！关于沙漠之脚，您肯定有些又怪、又重口的见解吧？

source: "My opinions are not 'kinky', nor 'wacky-assed,'" the attendee scoffs.
target: “我的见解，既不‘重口’，也不‘怪’。”与会者嗤道。

source: "My opinion of the Desert Foot is this: it's nature's monument to the most inspiring, aerodynamic appendage of the monster form."
target: “我对沙漠之脚的看法是：大自然立此丰碑，纪念怪物身体中，最启迪人心、最符合空气动力学的肢端。”

source: "It's a testament to the foot's durability, the vital role it plays in our locomotion, and its contribution to sports, dance, and the shoe industry."
target: “见证脚的坚韧，脚对行走的重要作用，以及脚为运动、舞蹈、鞋业，作出的贡献。”

source: That's really cool, bro! I gotta admit, I never thought about it that way.
target: 真酷，兄弟！说真的，从来没这样想过。

source: I thought people who were into feet were just horny about it.
target: 还以为，喜欢脚的人，都只是馋脚呢。

source: "Well, I won't lie. Feet also make me really fuckin' horny. But I know how not to be weird about it in everyday conversation."
target: “不瞒你说，脚也真他妈让我欲火焚身。不过，平时聊天，我知道怎么不让人觉得怪。”

source: Yeah, I understand that; I'm the same way with guac.
target: 懂，我对鳄梨酱，也这样。

source: Maybe I could learn to appreciate the beauty of the foot myself! I'll try anything once.
target: 说不定，我也能学着欣赏脚的美。什么都愿意试一次！

source: Wait, is public opinion suddenly swinging in favor of the foot fetishists now?
target: 等等，风向突然变了，现在大家都支持恋足爱好者了？

source: I guess so. It's like they say: don't knock it 'til you try it!
target: 好像是。俗话说，没试过，先别嫌弃嘛！

source: Fine, you'll give it a go. You've been devoted to weirder things than feet!
target: 行，你试试。比脚更怪的东西，你都痴迷过。

source: Will you lose -N2 SOUL for exaggerating your interests just to fit in? Yes, but you'll be popular, and that's all that matters!
target: 为了合群，夸大兴趣，会让你损失-N2灵魂吗？会，不过，受欢迎，才最重要！

source: You just have to come up with a way to show your passion for feet that'll impress your friends and the Afeetcionados!
target: 只要想个办法，展现对脚的热情，让朋友们和足迷，都刮目相看！

source: "I'm starting a class action lawsuit against football as a sport for being misleading on the involvement of feet in the whole thing."
target: “我要对美式橄榄球，提起集体诉讼！英文叫‘脚球’，脚却没那么重要，这名字，误导消费者。”

source: "When I read books, I only read the footnotes."
target: “读书，我只读脚注。”

source: "Hey, that's great!" says the foot-loving guy. "I was also duped by football's misleading name, like many others. It's high time someone did something about it!"
target: “太棒了！”爱脚的男人说，“不只我，好多人都被橄榄球这名字骗了。早该有人，管管了！”

source: You schedule the trial for later that day, because nobody has time for sensible due process.
target: 你把开庭时间，定在当天晚些时候。谁有空，走什么合理的正当程序。

source: The trial is wild. The prosecutor grills the CEO of Football for hours. "OBJECTION!" is shouted several times. The surprise witness caught everyone off guard.
target: 庭审精彩纷呈。检察官盘问橄榄球首席执行官，足足几小时。“反对！”喊了好几轮。出人意料的证人，更杀了所有人一个措手不及。

source: Things aren't looking good. You're gonna need some last-minute surprise evidence to save this case...
target: 情况不妙，得在最后关头，拿出意外的关键证据，救救这案子……

source: Which you have, of course, 'cause courtroom drama things.
target: 当然，你有。法庭剧，就得这样。

source: YOUR HONOR! I offer you this security tape from the CEO of Football's meeting room, taken from the night that they named football!
target: 法官大人！我提交的，是橄榄球首席执行官会议室的监控！就在决定“脚球”这名字，那晚录的！

source: "NOOOOO!" wails the CEO. "I should've known it was a bad idea to set up a security camera in my own evil plan room!"
target: “不——！”首席执行官哀号，“早该知道，在自己的邪恶计划室装监控，准没好事！”

source: The tape rolls. "Let's name this sport to cater to a taboo, niche market," says the CEO on camera. "Those demographics pay the most money for the dumbest shit."
target: 录像开始。“给这运动起名，要迎合禁忌小众市场。”画面里，首席执行官说道，“那些人，最肯为蠢东西，花大钱。”

source: "Okay! What about... scat-play-ball?"
target: “好啊！那叫……玩屎球？”

source: "Ew. We said 'taboo and niche', Rick, not 'total freaks.'"
target: “呕。里克，说的是‘禁忌小众’，不是‘彻头彻尾的变态’。”

source: "I'm thinking 'football.' It's just close enough to sounding like a sport, while still tricking the dumb foot lovers!"
target: “我想叫‘脚球’。听着够像运动，又能骗过，那群傻傻的爱脚人士！”

source: "It's foolproof! I mean, what are they gonna do, SUE US?! Ahahahaha!"
target: “万无一失！难道，他们还能告我们？！啊哈哈哈！”

source: Oof. Hindsight sure is 20/20.
target: 啧，事后回看，果然都明白了。

source: Yay, the judge ruled in our favor! Now Football has 72 hours to change its name to something more accurate to the actual sport. Good work, team!
target: 好耶，法官判我们赢！橄榄球，现在得在72小时内，换个更符合实际的名字。干得好，团队！

source: Three days later, America's favorite pastime is now known as "Dickpunchball." Democracy is a beautiful thing.
target: 三天后，全美最爱的消遣，改名叫“捶屌球”。民主，真美好。

source: The Afeetcionados also get a fat reparations payout, and you get a +N2 MONEY cut!
target: 足迷们，还拿到大笔赔偿，你也分到了+N2金钱！

source: Footnotes, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%? Really? Not exactly the pinnacle of cool. (I)
target: 脚注，%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%？真的？不太酷啊。（I）

source: I never read the footnotes, personally. They hurt my head, and I get dizzy even looking at them. (II)
target: 我反正从不读脚注。头疼，光看，都晕。（II）

source: Yeah. If you want this road trip to be fun, boo, why do you bring up boring shit all the time? (III) Let's go, I'm over this.
target: 亲爱的，想让公路旅行好玩，怎么还老提无聊东西？（III）走吧，没劲。

source: FOOTNOTE I: While Polly may have sounded dismissive when you said you "weren't the pinnacle of cool", she was actually utilizing subtle linguistic irony.
target: 脚注I：那句“不够酷”，也许让波莉显得有点轻蔑，其实，她在运用微妙的语言反讽。

source: She said you're "not cool" because she thinks you're "smoking hot", obviously!
target: 说你“不酷”，当然是因为，觉得你“辣到冒烟”！

source: FOOTNOTE II: Scott claims that reading the footnotes gives him a headache, but that's just the feeling of learning, a sensation Scott is not used to.
target: 脚注II：斯科特说，读脚注头疼。那只是学习的感觉，斯科特还不习惯而已。

source: But you are used to it, and you gain +N2 MIND by exercising your brain here in the footnotes!
target: 你可习惯。在脚注里动动脑，你就获得了+N2头脑！

source: FOOTNOTE III: Polly is WRONG about you making the road trip boring. Everyone's having a great time, she's just too stubborn to admit it.
target: 脚注III：波莉说，你让旅途无聊，她错了。大家都玩得很开心，她就是嘴硬，不肯认。

source: Trust me. I'm the footnotes, filled with definitions and credible citations*, and I would never lie!
target: 信我。我是脚注，写满定义，还有可靠引文*，绝不骗人！

source: *Narrator, The. "I Said This So It Is True", 'Narrator's Thoughts', pp. 69 (nice).
target: *旁白：《我说了，所以是真的》，载《旁白随想》，第69页（嘿嘿）。

source: Benefit from the potato
target: 从土豆身上获益

source: You and your friends are admiring this agricultural giant when you announce your intent to "benefit from the potato."
target: 你们正欣赏这位农作物巨人，你忽然宣布，要“从土豆身上获益”。

source: Benefit? No idea what that means, but it has "fit" in it, so it must be a good thing, right?
target: “获益”？没懂，可有个“益”字，肯定有益健康吧？

source: You betcha, Scott! It means we're gonna make some sweet profit off this potato. Let's pretend to be tour guides and make up funny stuff about the potato!
target: 当然，斯科特！意思是，从土豆身上，好好捞一笔。咱们假扮导游，编些好笑的土豆知识！

source: Sounds fun! Who are we gonna prank?
target: 好玩！这回整谁？

source: Ahh, the mighty potato! A wonderful tuber, second only to the yam. Yams get first place because they go great with marshmallows.
target: 啊，伟大的土豆！多好的块茎，只比红薯差点。红薯排第一，因为配棉花糖，太好吃了。

source: I personally dislike how they cook these things in so many ways: smashed, puréed, grilled, baked... can't you just stick to one thing and be good at it?
target: 我不喜欢，这东西弄出那么多做法：捣碎、打泥、炙烤、烘焙……专心干一件事，把它干好，不行吗？

source: I miss the good ol' days, when people just shoved perfectly good raw potatoes in their mouths and shut up.
target: 怀念以前，人们拿个好好的生土豆，往嘴里一塞，就闭嘴了。

source: Well, I guess this is a potayto-potahto situation, isn't it? Hahaha!
target: 看来，是“土豆、马铃薯，不都一样”嘛？哈哈哈！

source: ...It isn't.
target: ……并不是。

source: Hi Coach! Hi Camp Director Miss Weaving! What are you guys doing here?
target: 嗨，教练！嗨，营地主任织布小姐！你们怎么来了？

source: Oh, not much. Just enjoying one of the only weeks of my life when I don't have to hear anyone call me "Camp Director." Yourselves?
target: 哦，没什么。享受难得不用听人叫“营地主任”的休假，这辈子，没几周这种日子。你们呢？

source: We're volunteer tour guides for the Big Potato. I'm getting internship credit for it. I was thinking about majoring in French fries in college.
target: 我们是大马铃薯的志愿导游，还能拿实习学分。我想，上大学，主修薯条。

source: That's great, kiddo! Never stop setting goals for yourself!
target: 太好了，孩子！永远别停下，给自己定目标！

source: Wanna hear a cool potato fact? A potato this size could've stopped the Irish famine! Well, maybe not STOPPED, but it would've at least slowed it down a bit.
target: 想听个酷酷的土豆知识？这么大的土豆，能阻止爱尔兰大饥荒！好吧，不一定阻止，至少，能稍微缓缓。

source: Here's one! Potatoes only grow underground! Except for this one, I guess, since it's above ground. That's what makes the Big Potato so special!
target: 我也来一个！土豆，只在地下长！除了这个，毕竟，它在地上。大马铃薯，就特别在这儿！

source: Mr. Howl, has it occurred to you that perhaps they simply dug the potato out of the ground so we could see it?
target: 嚎尔先生，有没有可能，是把土豆，从地下挖出来，才给我们看的？

source: ...Holy shit.
target: ……卧槽。

source: Okay, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%, I'm passing you the ball while Scott hits the bench. Gimme a real slam-dunk of a potato fact!
target: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，球传给你，斯科特，先坐板凳。来条土豆知识，给我扣个漂亮篮！

source: "Although potatoes may seem rare, they're secretly hidden in a lot of common foods, such as French fries or chips! Not in fish, though. Fish are NOT made of potato."
target: “土豆看着稀有，其实，藏在很多常见食物里，比如薯条和薯片！不过鱼不是，鱼可不是土豆做的。”

source: "Vodka is made of potatoes. Therefore, if you eat enough potatoes, you'll get very drunk."
target: “伏特加，是土豆做的。所以，土豆吃够了，就能醉得不行。”

source: "Little-known fact: potatoes scare alligators. And now you can purchase this bag full of ketchup-flavored anti-alligator talismans!"
target: “冷知识，土豆能吓跑鳄鱼。现在，这袋番茄酱味防鳄护身符，欢迎选购！”

source: Whoa! I didn't know fries and chips were made of potatoes. I've been getting a lot more of my daily vegetables than I thought!
target: 哇，薯条、薯片，居然是土豆做的？原来我每天，吃的蔬菜，比想象中多这么多！

source: Yup! You know what else is made of potatoes? Vodka! So I'm also getting all my veggies.
target: 对！还有什么，是土豆做的？伏特加！所以我的蔬菜，也吃够了。

source: Indeed! And you were right; fish are certainly NOT made out of potatoes.
target: 没错！你说得对，鱼，确实不是土豆做的。

source: Happy to see your potato facts are on point! Maybe I did a good job with you kids in the end!
target: 真高兴，土豆知识都对！看来，对你们这些孩子，我教得还不错！

source: What do you mean by that? You're their sports coach, not their... potato teacher?
target: 什么意思？你是体育教练，又不是他们的……土豆老师？

source: And anyway, is it really a good idea to praise them for knowledge of such basic trivia? Everybody knows fish aren't made of potatoes.
target: 而且，这么基础的常识，也值得夸？鱼不是土豆做的，谁不知道。

source: Hey, not EVERYBODY knows that, okay? You don't need to be mean about it!
target: 喂，也不是所有人，都知道的，好吗？不用这么刻薄吧！

source: Aww, it's okay, Scott. Maybe we can come up with a way to help you remember what's made of potatoes and what isn't made of potatoes.
target: 没事，斯科特。咱们想个办法，帮你记住，哪些东西是土豆做的，哪些不是。

source: What about a website? Like a "potato or not potato" search engine?
target: 做个网站呢？“土豆不土豆”搜索引擎？

source: You could type in a thing, and the site will tell you if it's made of potatoes or not! BOOM!
target: 输个东西进去，网站就告诉你，是不是土豆做的！搞定！

source: That sounds like a million dollar idea!
target: 这主意，值一百万！

source: That sounds like a terrible idea. Can't you focus on doing something profitable, like becoming a lawyer or a doctor?
target: 这主意，糟透了。专心做点能赚钱的，比如当律师、医生，不行吗？

source: If I stay here any longer, I'll need a vacation from this vacation... Coach, can we go look for a diner? I need a glass of wine, or twelve.
target: 再待下去，这趟假期结束，我还得再休个假……教练，去找家餐厅吧，我得喝杯酒，或者十二杯。

source: Okie-dokie! I'm suddenly craving some fish and chips anyway!
target: 好嘞！反正，突然想吃炸鱼薯条了！

source: Bye, kiddos! Never stop chasing your potato-themed dreams!
target: 再见，孩子们！土豆主题的梦想，永远别放弃！

source: Well, that prank was a bit underwhelming. You lose -N2 HYPE, but you gain +N2 MIND from learning what is and isn't made of potatoes!
target: 这恶作剧，确实不怎么带劲，你损失-N2热度。不过，学会哪些是土豆做的，哪些不是，让你获得+N2头脑！

source: Wow, I never knew that! I admit that I'm not much of a vodka connoisseur, though.
target: 哇，以前真不知道！不过，说实话，伏特加，我也不怎么懂。

source: I'll have a cocktail at the Spooky Academy faculty holiday parties, but not much else. Who knew I could streamline the process by just eating a potato!
target: 惊悚学院教职工过节聚会，我会喝杯鸡尾酒，其他时候，基本不喝。谁知道，直接吃土豆，还能省事呢！

source: Don't buy into it, Coach. I think this "fun fact" is just a "hip prank" these kids want to play on their elders. For shame!
target: 教练，别信。我看，这“趣闻”，就是孩子们用来戏弄长辈的“潮流恶作剧”。丢人！

source: Really? You told me just the other day that you don't eat potatoes much. Are you 100% certain that this fun fact was, in fact, false?
target: 真的？前两天，你不还说，不常吃土豆？百分之百确定，这知识，是假的？

source: Ugh... I admit, I can't speak from experience on this subject.
target: 呃……这事，我确实没亲身经验。

source: Then you shouldn't be so confident about something you've never tried! Most of life's lessons have to be learned by dribbling a mile in the rival team's court.
target: 没试过，就别那么肯定嘛！人生的大部分道理，都得去对手的球场，运上一英里的球，才能懂。

source: Fine. If you want to eat a bunch of potatoes in an attempt to get drunk, be my guest.
target: 行吧，想吃一堆土豆，把自己吃醉，随你。

source: I'm going to see if the gift shop carries novelty 4-armed T-shirts in a size medium.
target: 我去看看礼品店，有没有中码的四臂搞怪 T 恤。

source: Miss Weaving leaves. You, Scott, and Polly go to the adjacent diner with Coach and watch him eat an obscene amount of potatoes.
target: 织布小姐走了。你、斯科特和波莉，陪教练去旁边餐厅，看他吃下，离谱数量的土豆。

source: Whoo! I feel... something. It's been so long since I've actually been drunk.
target: 呼！有点……感觉了。真是，好久没喝醉过了。

source: I shouldn't overdo it. I think this old tiger has had enough potatoes for one day!
target: 不能过量。我这老虎，今天的土豆，已经够了！

source: Say, kids, I'd rather you not tell the school about this. It's not a great look for me to be imbibing alcohol in front of my students.
target: 孩子们，别告诉学校。在学生面前喝酒，总归不太好看。

source: But just between us, here's a bag of potato chips. Just remember to consume potatoes responsibly and don't drive afterwards! Enjoy your youth!
target: 不过，咱们私下说，薯片拿好。土豆，吃得有分寸，吃完也别开车！享受青春吧！

source: You lose -N2 SOUL for tricking Coach into thinking he's drunk; yet you conversely gain +N2 HYPE for tricking Coach into thinking he's drunk. Cool!
target: 骗教练相信，自己喝醉了，让你损失-N2灵魂；可骗教练相信，自己喝醉了，又让你获得+N2热度。酷！

source: That's... wow. I'm genuinely stunned by how idiotic that claim was.
target: 这……哇。能蠢到这份上，真是，把我震住了。

source: What, are you saying we're wrong? Do you see any alligators around right now?
target: 什么，意思是，我们说错了？看看周围，有鳄鱼吗？

source: Of course not! It's 'cause they're scared of the big potato. Checkmate.
target: 当然没有！怕大土豆嘛。将军。

source: Fascinating, I never knew! Thank you kids for reminding me, every day, that a mentor can also learn things from his mentees. You were the real Coach today!
target: 神奇，真没听过！孩子们，天天提醒我，老师也能向学生学习。今天，你们才是真正的教练！

source: I'll buy those ketchup-flavored alligator talismans from ya. I'll always support your passions -- and you never know when you'll face some hungry alligators!
target: 番茄酱味防鳄护身符，我买。你们的热情，我永远支持。再说，谁知道什么时候，会碰上饿鳄鱼！

source: You gain +N2 MONEY and +N4 HYPE for your great, profitable prank! But you lose -N2 STAMINA for giving away your chips.
target: 精彩又赚钱的恶作剧，让你获得+N2金钱和+N4热度。不过，薯片给出去了，你也损失了-N2体力。

source: You also lose -N4 SOUL for taking advantage of Coach -- or DID you take advantage of him? A few days later...
target: 占教练便宜，还让你损失-N4灵魂。不过，真占便宜了吗？几天后……

source: I can't believe we're being chased by hungry alligators at the World's Lowest-Security Alligator Farm! What were the odds?!
target: 真没想到，在“全世界安保最差鳄鱼养殖场”，会被饿鳄鱼追！这概率，多小啊？！

source: Don't worry, Coach! I have a pistol in my purse. You run for help, I'll light the bastards up!
target: 别怕，教练！包里有枪。你去求救，我轰了这群混蛋！

source: No way am I leaving a soldier behind! I have those anti-alligator talismans with me! I told you they'd come in handy!
target: 绝不丢下战友！防鳄护身符，我带着呢！早说了，能派上用场！

source: Miss Weaving shoots at the alligators, and Coach throws potato chips everywhere. The gators retreat!
target: 织布小姐朝鳄鱼开枪，教练到处撒薯片。鳄鱼退了！

source: Whew! Thank goodness we're safe...
target: 呼！还好，安全了……

source: Indeed. We're so lucky I kept those anti-alligator talismans all this time!
target: 幸好，我一直留着，这些防鳄护身符！

source: What? No, it was the gun that saved us. The gators retreated because I shot at them.
target: 什么？不是，救命的是枪。我开枪，鳄鱼才退的。

source: Well, I guess this is a potayto-GUNtahto situation, isn't it?
target: 看来，是“土豆、马铃枪，不都一样”嘛？

source: I swear to God if you make that joke one more time...
target: 我发誓，你再讲一次这笑话……

source: Hahaha!
target: 哈哈哈！

source: Research the potato
target: 研究土豆

source: You decide to learn more about the potato. But as you're reaching for some informational brochures, a trenchcoat-wearing rando grabs your wrist!
target: 你想多了解点土豆，正伸手拿介绍册，突然，一个穿风衣的陌生人，抓住你的手腕！

source: "You lookin' for info about the potato?" he whispers. "Don't waste your time with their brochures. If you want the truth, follow the white rabbit."
target: “想查土豆？”他压低声音，“别浪费时间，看他们的册子。想知道真相，就跟着白兔走。”

source: I love chasing rabbits, but there's, like, a TON of white rabbits in the world, bro. Which one are we supposed to follow?
target: 追兔子，我喜欢，可世上白兔，多着呢。兄弟，跟哪只？

source: "What? No, don't literally follow a rabbit. You gotta follow the METAPHORICAL rabbit."
target: “什么？不是让你真去追兔子。是比喻里的兔子！”

source: Okaaay... are you referring to the white rabbit tattoo on your neck? Is it you we're supposed to follow? 'Cause that isn't what a metaphor is.
target: 哦——说的是，你脖子上，那个白兔纹身？要跟着你走？可那，不叫比喻。

source: "Yes! That was a test, and you passed it. That means I can trust you with this knowledge: the Big Potato is a CONSPIRACY!"
target: “对！测试而已，你通过了。现在，这秘密，能告诉你了：大马铃薯，是个阴谋！”

source: NO. WAY.
target: 不。是。吧。

source: "Yes way! Check out my forum where I post all of my theories about the potato. You're just one click away from unveiling the truth..."
target: “就是！我把土豆的所有理论，都发在论坛上。只要点一下，真相就在眼前……”

source: "Well hello there, young folk!" a nearby kindly old man says. It's the farmer who grew the potato! "What brings you to my humble little farm?"
target: “年轻人，你们好！”旁边，一位和蔼老人开口了。正是种出土豆的农夫！“什么风，把各位吹到小农场来？”

source: "Drop the act, old man!" shouts the conspiracy nut. "I'm onto your game! Like potatoes, this conspiracy has many layers, but I'm gonna bust it wide open!"
target: “别装了，老头！”阴谋论狂人喊道，“看穿你了！这阴谋，像土豆一样，层层叠叠，可我一定，要把它彻底揭开！”

source: Onions have layers, not potatoes. You SUCK at literary comparisons, dude.
target: 层层叠叠的是洋葱，不是土豆。兄弟，比喻，你烂透了。

source: Suddenly, the farmer pulls out a gun and shoots the conspiracy theorist 4 times in the chest! Then he points the gun at you all!
target: 农夫突然掏枪，对着阴谋论者的胸口，连开四枪！随后，枪口指向你们！

source: "Sorry, kids, but I can't let the potato conspiracy get out," he says. "It's a shame, but I gotta kill ya."
target: “抱歉，孩子们，土豆阴谋，不能泄露。”他说，“可惜了，得杀你们。”

source: But we didn't even get to check that weirdo's blog! We know nothing about the potato other than that it's big. So are we good?
target: 可那怪人的博客，都还没看呢！土豆除了大，我们什么也不知道。所以，没事吧？

source: "Oh, oops... but you all saw me murder that guy, and that's a loose thread. I can't leave y'all alive."
target: “哦，糟了……可你们看见我杀人，也算后患，不能留活口。”

source: Nooo, you promised your mom you wouldn't die today! Talk the farmer out of killing you! Convince him you won't tell anyone what happened!
target: 不行啊，答应过妈妈，今天不死！快劝农夫，别杀你们，保证不把事情，说出去！

source: Tell the farmer your most embarrassing secret: you don't know exactly where your anus is.
target: 坦白你最丢人的秘密：你不知道，自己肛门到底在哪儿。

source: Let the farmer record a video of you saying that you will murder the President to give him immense leverage against you.
target: 让农夫给你录视频，声称准备谋杀总统，给他足够的把柄，制住你。

source: What? How do you not know that? Don't you have an anus, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%?
target: 什么？这都不知道？%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，你没有肛门吗？

source: If you don't know where your butthole is, how do you go to the bathroom? Does the poop get lost and stay stuck inside you?
target: 屁眼在哪儿，都不清楚，怎么上厕所？屎会不会迷路，堵在里面？

source: Yes, obviously you have an anus, and you can poop, but it's not like you can look down and see your bootyhole when you sit on the toilet!
target: 当然有肛门，当然能拉屎。可坐马桶时，又不能低头，直接看见屁眼！

source: Through years of speculation and cautious experimentation, you've learned that it must be located SOMEWHERE below your waist. But beyond that, you're stumped.
target: 多年推理、谨慎实验后，你确定了：它肯定在腰部以下某处。再往下，就不知道了。

source: "WOW," says the farmer. "I'll be honest, kiddo: I wish I didn't know that. I miss the person that I was 10 seconds ago before you told me that."
target: “哇。”农夫说，“孩子，说真的，真希望没听见。我怀念十秒钟前，还不知道这事的自己。”

source: You and me both, pal... you and me both...
target: 彼此彼此，兄弟……彼此彼此……

source: "Okay, I think we have a deal here: you don't tell nobody about the murder, and I won't tell nobody that you don't know where your own asshole is. G'day, kids." He leaves.
target: “好，成交。你们不说杀人的事，我也不说，你不知道自己屁眼在哪儿。再见，孩子们。”他走了。

source: All right, gang, new rule: everyone on the road trip is required to know the location of their own anus. %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%, come watch this.
target: 各位，新规矩：参加公路旅行，必须知道自己肛门在哪儿。%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，过来看。

source: Polly shows you a playlist of recorded colonoscopies that she found online because... the internet, I guess.
target: 波莉打开，网上找的一整套肠镜录像。因为……这就是互联网吧。

source: You still aren't 100% sure where the anus is; colonoscopies do a better job of teaching you where the anus is from inside the body than the outside...
target: 你还是不完全清楚，肛门在哪儿。肠镜录像，教得好的是体内视角，可不是从外面看……

source: But after the sixth video you tell your friends you know now, so you can stop this.
target: 不过，第六段之后，你告诉朋友们，懂了，免得再看下去。

source: You lose -N2 HYPE by weirding out your friends, but later that night you finally check that potato conspiracy blog... and trust me, what you read earns you +N2 MIND.
target: 你把朋友们，恶心了一把，损失-N2热度。不过，晚上，你终于看了那个土豆阴谋博客。相信我，内容足够让你+N2头脑。

source: WOW. Uh, gotta say, you jumped from "don't kill me" to "I'll murder the President in cold blood" VERY quickly.
target: 哇。从“别杀我”，跳到“我会冷血地谋杀总统”，你这转得，可真快。

source: "Hmmm, that'd work," the farmer says. "Such a bold threat would give me plenty of reassurance that you won't go squeal on me."
target: “嗯，这办法行。”农夫说，“这么大胆的威胁，能让我放心，你不会去告发我。”

source: Okay, we're doing this, I guess.
target: 行吧，看来，得这么干了。

source: The farmer sets up his camera. He hits record, and you say, "I, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%, am going to murder the President."
target: 农夫架好相机，按下录制。你说：“我，%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，准备谋杀总统。”

source: Hmm, I'm not convinced. %CURRENTPLAYERNAME% looks too harmless! Maybe %HESHE%'d look more evil if %HESHE% wore an eyepatch?
target: 嗯，没信服。%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%太人畜无害了！%HESHE%要是戴个眼罩，%HESHE%是不是就邪恶多了？

source: Why would wearing an eyepatch make %CURRENTPLAYERNAME% evil?
target: 戴眼罩，怎么就让%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%邪恶了？

source: Tired movie stereotypes, Scott. On any other day we should ditch them; but today we're making a terrorism-adjacent video, so fuck it, eyepatch it is!
target: 老掉牙的电影刻板印象，斯科特。平时，该扔掉，可今天，录的是恐怖威胁边缘的视频。管他呢，戴眼罩！

source: You try it with the eyepatch on. It doesn't entirely work, perhaps because an eyepatch isn't directly related to someone's morality.
target: 你试着戴上眼罩，还是不太行。也许，因为眼罩，跟一个人的道德，根本没直接关系。

source: Maybe the problem is the cinematography. Try filming it at a Dutch tilt angle to accentuate the surrealism.
target: 也许，是摄影有问题。用倾斜镜头拍，突出超现实感。

source: And I want more pathos, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%! I want to taste the blood in your words!
target: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，情绪，再强烈点！我要从你的话里，尝到血腥味！

source: Picture the president stealing your favorite hat. He campaigned and got to office only to have enough influence to get your hat. Work with that!
target: 想象，总统偷走你最爱的帽子。竞选、上任，就为权势够大，能拿走这帽子。带着这感觉演！

source: Let's do two eyepatches! Double the evil!
target: 两只眼罩！双倍邪恶！

source: Great, now a homicidal stranger has a video of you threatening the President while totally blind. This can't go wrong.
target: 真好。杀人狂陌生人手里，多了一段你双眼全蒙着，威胁总统的视频。绝对不会出事。

source: "Well... it ain't 'Casablanca', but it'll work fine for blackmail material," says the farmer. "Nice meetin' you folks!"
target: “算不上《卡萨布兰卡》，不过，勒索，够用了。”农夫说，“认识各位，真高兴！”

source: You've lost your dignity and -N2 SOUL from threatening the president. But you gain +N2 MIND when you check the conspiracy nut's potato blog later that night.
target: 威胁总统，赔上了尊严，还让你损失-N2灵魂。不过，晚上看了那阴谋论狂人的土豆博客，你获得+N2头脑。

source: You don't get much from it, since you're still wearing the two eyepatches. But Polly and Scott assure you that it's mind-blowing!
target: 你其实没看懂多少，毕竟，还戴着两只眼罩。不过，波莉和斯科特保证，惊掉下巴！

source: Feed from the potato
target: 从土豆上找吃的

source: How could you look at a giant potato and NOT crave fries?! You need to find something to eat.
target: 这么大一颗土豆，谁看了不馋薯条？！得找点吃的。

source: Hey, look! They have a diner built into the side of the potato!
target: 嘿，快看！餐厅，直接嵌在土豆侧面！

source: Ugh, that's a long line. They'd better at least have vodka on the menu...
target: 呃，队好长。菜单上，最好至少有伏特加……

source: Welcome to the Big Potato Diner. What can I get you?
target: 欢迎光临大马铃薯餐厅。要点什么？

source: One hamburger, please!
target: 请来一个汉堡！

source: ...What part of "potato diner" don't you understand?
target: ……“土豆餐厅”，哪几个字，没听懂？

source: Don't ask him that. We might be here for a while.
target: 别问他这个，不然，得聊半天。

source: Damn, these dishes are kinda expensive. Why's this potato stand so pricey?
target: 妈的，菜还挺贵。土豆摊，怎么卖这么贵？

source: Because we make all our food out of the Big Potato. "Every bite is a bite of Potato History (TM)."
target: 所有食物，都拿大马铃薯做。“每一口，都在品味土豆历史（TM）。”

source: Awesome! Does the Big Potato make really good potato dishes or something?
target: 酷！拿大马铃薯做的土豆菜，是特别好吃吗？

source: Ehh, if anything they all taste kinda stale. The Big Potato's getting a little up there in age...
target: 呃，硬要说，都有点不新鲜。大马铃薯，年纪不小了……

source: But hey, we have this special section on the menu. The manager isn't sure if it's morally okay to keep selling these dishes, so the prices are more competitive.
target: 不过，菜单上还有个特价区。经理不确定，继续卖这些菜，道德上说不说得过去，所以，价格更有竞争力。

source: That doesn't sound great, but oh boy, these prices are low! They're so cheap, they won't even make a dent in your MONEY!
target: 听着不太妙，可价格，真低！便宜到，你的金钱数值，都不会动！

source: The question is, which of these dishes will feed you while fucking you up in the least inconvenient way?
target: 问题是，哪道菜，既能让你吃饱，又能尽量，少给你添点麻烦？

source: The Infinite Fry
target: 无限薯条

source: Smashed Potatoes
target: 砸碎土豆

source: It isn't LITERALLY infinite, is it? There's no way to finish cooking something that defies the laws of time and space.
target: 不是真无限吧？违反时空定律的东西，哪有办法，彻底煮熟？

source: Sure. For legal purposes, it's not infinite. Just try not to think too much about it and stop eating it at some point and you should be fine.
target: 当然，从法律上说，它不无限。别想太多，吃着吃着，记得找个时候停下，就没事。

source: You start eating. You gain +N2 STAMINA. You chew and chew, thinking at any moment you'll reach the end of the fry... but you don't.
target: 你开吃，获得+N2体力。一口又一口，总觉得，再咬一下，就该吃到这根薯条的头了……可就是没有。

source: You eat that same fry for one minute, then five minutes, then an hour, then longer... there's no end to this crunchy, salty... thing.
target: 同一根薯条，你吃了一分钟，五分钟，一小时，还更久……这香脆、咸咸的东西，根本没有尽头。

source: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%, I'm sorry, but it's time for an intervention. You gotta stop eating that fry. It's unhealthy for you!
target: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，抱歉，可得管管你了。别再吃，这对你不好！

source: No way! I've invested too much time into finishing this fry now. I HAVE to see it through. Sunk cost fallacy for the win!
target: 不行！都花这么久，要吃完这根薯条，我必须坚持到底。沉没成本谬误，万岁！

source: Can we at least have some...?
target: 至少，分我们一点……？

source: NO! IT'S MY FRY!
target: 不！我的薯条！

source: You keep eating, but your brain cannot comprehend infinity, not even in such starchy, simplistic terms. You eventually pass out.
target: 你继续吃。可脑子，终究理解不了无限，哪怕它只是这么简单、充满淀粉的东西。最后，你晕了。

source: You wake up in the car. Scott and Polly threw the fry away and took you here to take care of you, which was nice of them.
target: 你在车里醒来。斯科特和波莉，把薯条扔了，带你来休息，好好照顾，真贴心。

source: But you're kinda upset, because you'd finally found your true calling: eating that Infinite Fry to completion! Your purpose in life, gone forever...
target: 可你有点不爽。刚找到人生使命：吃完那根无限薯条！活着的意义，就这么，永远没了……

source: You lose -N2 MIND, and occasionally suffer from nightmares that make you wake up in cold sweats, looking all starch... STARK! Looking all stark! Goddammit...
target: 你损失-N2头脑，偶尔还做噩梦，吓得冷汗惊醒，惊魂未“淀”——定！惊魂未定！妈的……

source: Sounds yummy! I love mashed potatoes!
target: 听着好吃！我爱土豆泥！

source: No, these are different. These are SMASHED potatoes.
target: 不一样，这是“砸碎”土豆。

source: What's the difference? Potayto-potahto, am I right?
target: 差在哪儿？土豆、马铃薯，不都一样嘛？

source: Sure. I definitely don't hear that ten times a day. %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%, come with me.
target: 对，绝对不是每天，都能听见十次的笑话。%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，跟我来。

source: The server hands you a bib and a big, spiked club. Okay, THAT is definitely something you don't usually see alongside mashed potatoes.
target: 服务员递来围嘴，还有根大狼牙棒。嗯，这东西，确实不太会跟普通土豆泥，一起上桌。

source: She leads you all to the back, where you find an enclosure full of scared, scampering potato-creatures!
target: 她带你们去后面，围栏里，全是惊恐乱窜的土豆生物！

source: Pick the one you wanna eat and smash it to death. I'll sprinkle some rosemary on it for ya.
target: 想吃哪只，就把它砸死。我再给你，撒点迷迭香。

source: But... why? Just why?!
target: 可……为什么？到底为什么？！

source: Some rich folks like to choose their meal while it's still alive, no? Our manager took it a step further, and now we let the customers kill their meal themselves.
target: 有钱人，不喜欢挑活的吃吗？经理更进一步，让客人自己，杀自己的饭。

source: It's surprisingly popular. Guess there are more fucked-up people in this world than we could've imagined.
target: 没想到，还挺受欢迎。世上变态，比想象中多。

source: Isn't it possible, if not likely, that those people didn't actually want to club a sentient potato to death? Maybe they just made the same "smashed/mashed" mistake we did?
target: 有没有可能，他们也不想，把有意识的土豆活活砸死？只是跟我们一样，把“砸碎”，当成“捣碎”了？

source: Huh... that would make sense, actually. We had a big increase in "emotional trauma" lawsuits when we started serving Smashed Potatoes...
target: 嗯……倒有道理。开始供应砸碎土豆后，告我们“精神创伤”的案子，确实多了不少……

source: We'll rethink the menu item. You're still having smashed potatoes, though.
target: 我们会重新考虑这道菜。不过，你们这顿，还是砸碎土豆。

source: I already put the order in the system, and changing it is a whole process I don't feel like doing right now.
target: 订单已经录进系统，改起来，麻烦一大堆，现在不想弄。

source: The delicious and starchy +N2 STAMINA you get doesn't manage to wash away the -N2 SOUL from all the murder.
target: 香喷喷、满是淀粉的+N2体力，可洗不掉，因为杀戮而损失的-N2灵魂。

source: Was this a grim defeat or a yummy victory? That's up to you to decide.
target: 是惨痛的败仗，还是美味的胜利？你自己定。

source: Pull a prank
target: 玩个恶作剧

source: There are plenty of other visitors here, ripe for the pranking. You and your friends scope out your next target...
target: 游客这么多，个个都适合整。你和朋友们，物色起下一个目标……

source: Look, there's the hole! I love a good hole in the middle of the desert.
target: 看，那个洞！沙漠中央，有这么个好洞，真喜欢。

source: Who do you think dug it? I wonder if it started as a punishment. Ahh, the beautiful suffering of pointless manual labor!
target: 谁挖的呢？会不会，原本是惩罚？啊，毫无意义的体力劳动，多么美妙的折磨！

source: Want me to dig a bottomless hole for you, Miss Weaving? I could use the exercise anyway.
target: 织布小姐，要我给你挖个无底洞吗？反正，也能锻炼锻炼。

source: You'd dig a bottomless hole... just for me? Why, that's the nicest--
target: 专门为我……挖个无底洞？哎呀，从没见过这么体——

source: Hi, Coach! Hi, Camp Director Miss Weaving!
target: 嗨，教练！嗨，营地主任织布小姐！

source: You two seemed like you were having fun talking privately, so I wanted to butt in and have fun too!
target: 看你俩，私下聊得好开心，就想插进来，一起开心！

source: What Scott means to say is that we're... tour guides! Yeah, let's go with that! We're here to tell you fun facts about the hole!
target: 斯科特的意思是，我们是……导游！对，就这么说。给你们讲点，洞的趣闻！

source: Fun fact: holes play a big role in the three pillars of modern society: straws, gravedigging, and the donut industry.
target: 趣闻：现代社会三大支柱，吸管、挖坟、甜甜圈产业，都少不了洞！

source: Fun fact: I love digging holes! It's my favorite hobby!
target: 趣闻：我爱挖洞！最喜欢的爱好！

source: I know, Mr. Howl. We passed some of the holes you dug on the way here. It's a wonder we found the true landmark at all.
target: 嚎尔先生，我知道。来的路上，你挖的洞，见了好几个。还能找到真正的景点，都是奇迹。

source: Well, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%, Polly and Scott loaded the bases; now you're up to bat. Give us a real "hole in one" fun hole fact!
target: 好了，%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，波莉和斯科特，已经造好满垒局面，轮到你挥棒！讲条洞的趣闻，来个“一杆进洞”！

source: "This hole is so deep, you can most likely fit like... thirty pies in it."
target: “这洞，深得大概能装……三十个馅饼。”

source: "Many have argued the mysterious origins of the hole, but in reality it was a very weird marketing stunt pulled by a pizza place in the 80s."
target: “洞的神秘起源，向来众说纷纭。其实，是八十年代，一家披萨店搞的古怪营销活动。”

source: "If you listen carefully, the hole will whisper your darkest desires to you. Don't get confused if the hole sounds a lot like me. Sheer coincidence!"
target: “仔细听，洞会低语，道出你最黑暗的欲望。声音像我，别多想，纯属巧合！”

source: WHOA! That much?! I've never even SEEN thirty pies together, so I gotta assume that it's a lot!
target: 哇！这么多？！三十个馅饼，放在一起，见都没见过，肯定很多！

source: It is a lot, Scott! I wanna tell you how proud I am of how much better you've become at assumption-making.
target: 是很多，斯科特！你的推测能力，进步这么大，我真为你骄傲。

source: This is ridiculous! Pies are a terrible measurement for the depth of a hole!
target: 荒唐！馅饼，怎么能当测量洞深的单位！

source: Do you know for sure that they're a terrible measurement, though? Have you ever tested it?
target: 可确定不能吗？试过？

source: Well... no, I haven't. But I'm sure nobody else has either, due to the sheer stupidity of it all!
target: 好吧，没试过。可肯定，谁都没试，这太蠢了！

source: Nobody's tested it UNTIL TODAY! That's the scientific method: test your theories, write a paper about it, get a Nobel prize!
target: 直到今天，都没人试！科学方法，不就是验证理论、写论文、拿诺贝尔奖！

source: This probably isn't Nobel-winning research, but fuck it, you're in. Coach buys the pies, and you chuck them in the hole.
target: 大概拿不了诺贝尔奖，不过，管他呢，你加入了。教练买馅饼，你往洞里扔。

source: Cool! Your hypothesis was correct, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%. Thirty pies fit in the hole, with lots of room left over!
target: 酷！%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，你的假设对了。三十个馅饼，全装得下，还剩好多地方！

source: Wow! Do you think... thirty-ONE pies would fit in the hole?
target: 哇，那……三十一只，也装得下吗？

source: Sometimes we must accept that not all questions can be answered, Scott... and that's part of life's beauty.
target: 斯科特，有些问题，注定没有答案，得学会接受。人生之美，也在这里。

source: I can't watch this idiocy anymore. Coach, can we please go?
target: 这些蠢事，我看不下去了。教练，能走了吗？

source: Sure. Do you want to stop by a bakery? This face-hole of mine can surely fit at least ONE pie, haha!
target: 当然！要去趟面包店吗？我脸上这个洞，至少，能装一个馅饼，哈哈！

source: You gain +N2 MIND for your research! But you lose -N2 STAMINA because one of those pies was actually yours. Oh well!
target: 研究让你获得+N2头脑！不过，扔下去的馅饼，有一个其实是你的，你损失-N2体力。算了！

source: I have trouble believing that. Digging a hole in the middle of the desert seems like a terrible marketing ploy.
target: 很难相信。在沙漠中央挖洞，听着，就是糟糕的营销手段。

source: Oh, yeah, it was definitely a bad move. Cheapskate Cam's Pizza did a LOT of terrible marketing stunts before they finally shut down.
target: 对，确实糟糕。“小气鬼卡姆披萨店”，倒闭前，搞过好多烂营销。

source: They tried the hole, they did a sweepstakes where the winner got to name the CEO's firstborn child, they tried declaring oysters as the new cool side for pizza...
target: 挖过洞，还抽奖，让赢家给首席执行官的第一个孩子取名；也试过，把牡蛎捧成最潮的披萨配菜……

source: Fascinating stuff, kids! How come I've never heard of Cheapskate Cam's Pizza before?
target: 好有意思，孩子们！以前怎么没听过，小气鬼卡姆披萨店？

source: Are you really surprised? This was the company that thought digging a bottomless hole in the middle of the desert was better than just making a commercial.
target: 奇怪吗？这公司，可是觉得，沙漠里挖个无底洞，比直接拍条广告，还管用。

source: Honestly, it WAS the 80s. Chances are these marketing stunts were fueled by ludicrous amounts of coke.
target: 说真的，八十年代嘛。这种营销，大概都是嗑了海量可卡因，想出来的。

source: Well, Ms. Geist, I still think this story has... many holes in it.
target: 鬼斯特女士，这故事……漏洞，还是挺多的。

source: But I lived the 80s, and I saw several coked-up marketing stunts for overpriced fast food in my day, so the jury is still out.
target: 不过，八十年代，我也经历过。靠嗑药，想出天价快餐营销的，也没少见，暂且，不能下定论。

source: In any case, this is what happens when young folk stop cooking their meals AT HOME!
target: 总之，年轻人不肯在家做饭，就这后果！

source: Aww, I didn't know you liked homecooked meals!
target: 哎呀，原来喜欢家常菜啊！

source: Can I make you my famous lamb-heart-muscle-milk-vitamin-A smoothie sometime? It's great for your hamstrings!
target: 找天，给你做我拿手的，羊心肌肉奶维生素 A 奶昔？对腿后肌群，特别好！

source: Why... yes. That's thoughtful of you, Coach. I actually love consuming my food pureed.
target: 哎呀……好啊。教练，真体贴。我确实喜欢，把食物打成泥再吃。

source: Prank achieved! You get +N2 HYPE out of it! But you lose -N2 SOUL for deceiving people. Boo.
target: 恶作剧，成功！你获得+N2热度，不过，骗人也让你损失-N2灵魂。啧。

source: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%, you're an incompetent fool if you think we're gullible enough to--
target: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，以为我们，随便就会信，你可真是个无能的蠢——

source: HEY! BOTTOMLESS HOLE! TELL ME ALL MY DARKEST DESIRES!
target: 喂，无底洞！告诉我，全部最黑暗的欲望！

source: You stealthily lower yourself into the hole and whisper back:
target: 你悄悄溜下洞，压低声音回应：

source: Coach, your greatest desire is to buy Polly, Scott, and %CURRENTPLAYERNAME% burritos!
target: 教练，你最大的欲望，就是给波莉、斯科特和%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，买墨西哥卷饼！

source: That makes sense. Burritos aren't very healthy, but eating them is a dark, guilty pleasure of mine, and it'd be a pleasure to share a burrito with my students!
target: 有道理。卷饼不怎么健康，可吃它，就是我见不得光的内疚快乐。跟学生一起分享，更开心！

source: What else can you tell me, Hole? Do you have any predictions for my long-term deep, dark desires? My schedule's pretty clear next week.
target: 洞，还能告诉我什么？长期、深层、黑暗欲望，有什么预测？下周，时间挺空。

source: Coach, your even GREATEST-ER desire is to become a pro-skateboarder!
target: 教练，你更更更大的欲望，是当职业滑板选手！

source: It is? I had no idea! I've always respected skateboarding, but I never got into it because it lacked the quintessential sporty element: balls.
target: 是吗？还真不知道！一直尊重滑板，可没玩过，因为它缺了，体育最核心的元素：球。

source: But maybe my unshakeable loyalty to balls is actually a psychological dependence manifested from my unresolved issues with my father?
target: 也许，我对球的绝对忠诚，其实是心理依赖，源于跟父亲，那些尚未解决的问题？

source: Uh... sure?
target: 呃……算是吧？

source: Thank you, desert hole! It's been great unpacking my repressed memories with you. I'll pursue my secret dream of skateboarding!
target: 谢谢，沙漠洞！压抑的回忆，都梳理清楚了。我去追逐秘密的滑板梦！

source: The students are going to love it! I'll be so hip!
target: 学生们，肯定喜欢！我得多潮啊！

source: Hmm, do kids say hip anymore? I'll be so... "fleeky!"
target: 嗯，现在孩子，还说“潮”吗？我得……“潮到飞起”！

source: You lose -N6 SOUL for deeply invading Coach's privacy, but you gain +N2 MIND for mindfucking him and +N2 HYPE because PRANKS!
target: 深挖教练隐私，让你损失-N6灵魂。不过，精神上摆布他，让你获得+N2头脑；恶作剧嘛，还获得+N2热度！

source: And Coach takes you all out for burritos thanks to "the hole's" suggestion, so you also gain +N2 STAMINA!
target: 多亏“洞”的建议，教练带你们吃了卷饼，你又获得+N2体力！

source: Admire the hole
target: 欣赏这个洞

source: You all pick up guided audio tours from the gift shop and enjoy a tour of the hole together.
target: 你们在礼品店，各领一份语音导览，一起参观。

source: Polly, the nice British man on this tape says the first hole was dug OVER A MILLION YEARS AGO!
target: 波莉，录音里，那个亲切的英国男人说，第一个洞，是一百多万年前挖的！

source: I didn't know we even had that many years ago!
target: 都不知道，以前，居然有那么多年！

source: Man, check out this hole. This is a NICE hole, heh.
target: 瞧瞧，这洞，真是个好洞，嘿。

source: I thought staring into a bottomless pit of darkness would be existential and weird, but it's actually pretty chill.
target: 本以为，看无底的黑暗深渊，会古怪到，怀疑人生。没想到，还挺放松。

source: After the tour, you drop off your audio tours at the gate with the nice elderly couple who runs this place.
target: 参观完，你们到入口，把导览设备，还给经营这里的老两口。

source: Thanks for the cool hole, guys! It's been real!
target: 各位，谢了，这洞真酷！不虚此行！

source: They start to wave goodbye... then the old man bursts into tears!
target: 他们挥手告别……忽然，一位老先生，哭了！

source: Oh! Sorry! Was it something we said? Uh, it's been UN-real. Is that better?
target: 哦，抱歉！说错话了？呃，那……虚此行了？这样，好点？

source: "No, don't worry, you kids were great," the other old man sighs. "We wish we could find more visitors like you, to keep us from going bankrupt."
target: “不，别担心，孩子们，你们很好。”另一位老先生叹道，“要是能多些这样的客人，就不至于破产了。”

source: "We bought this hole forty years ago from a handsome entrepreneur who promised it'd make us rich and famous overnight."
target: “四十年前，一个英俊的创业者，把这个洞卖给我们，承诺能让我们，一夜暴富成名。”

source: You... bought a hole in a desert from a guy? Did he even dig it? I'm pretty sure some guy just scammed you into giving him money for a hole.
target: 你们……跟人买了个沙漠里的洞？他挖的吗？我看，是有个人，拿个洞，骗你们钱吧。

source: "Sure, but at first, our investment paid off! The bottomless hole was once what you kids might call 'the new Coachella!'"
target: “是啊，可最初，投资真有回报！这无底洞，一度就是你们年轻人说的，‘新科切拉’！”

source: "But now Coachella is the new Coachella, and none of the young folk come to see the hole anymore..."
target: “可现在，科切拉，才是新科切拉。年轻人，都不来看洞了……”

source: Look, we can help you get more customers I guess, but you GOTTA promise to invest your money better from now on.
target: 行，帮你们多找点客人，可以。不过，得保证，以后投资，靠谱点。

source: Sounds like a plan. Time to put on your business consultancy pants and help the old couple rebrand the hole to make it popular again!
target: 好，穿上商业顾问的裤子，帮老两口，给洞换个定位，重新火起来！

source: Market the hole to basic, crass dudebros who brag about having been in every hole.
target: 面向没品又粗俗的兄弟帮，专治他们“天下什么洞都进过”的吹牛。

source: Market the hole as the perfect starting point for very bad golfers.
target: 把洞包装成，菜鸟高尔夫选手的最佳起点。

source: Ugh... that's a cheap shot, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%. But, sadly, I think it'll probably work, even if it costs us -N2 SOUL.
target: 呃，%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，这招够低级。可惜，应该真管用，就算代价是-N2灵魂。

source: Well, they say sex sells. Looks like sexism sells too!
target: 性，能卖钱，原来，性别歧视也能！

source: Soon, dudes and bros and whole fraternities flock in from all over to claim their right to being in "every hole."
target: 很快，各路兄弟帮，连大学兄弟会，都从各地涌来，争着证明，自己“什么洞都进过”。

source: Wow, that worked quick. I guess bros really like digging holes!
target: 哇，好快！兄弟们，真爱挖洞啊！

source: It's not that. These guys just can't stand having their fragile masculinity shaken by being the butt of the joke.
target: 不是。他们那脆弱的男子气概，受不了被人当笑柄。

source: They HAVE to be able to say they've "been in every hole." It's dumb.
target: 非得说自己，“什么洞都进过”。蠢透了。

source: Hey, Scott! Good to see our little cousin here! Now we've ALL been in every hole!
target: 嘿，斯科特！咱家小老表，也在！这下，所有人，都什么洞都进过了！

source: Broooos! You here to admire the big hole too? Wanna bury some bones in it?
target: 兄弟们！也来看大洞？一起往里面埋骨头？

source: Daaaamn, little Scotty wants to bone the hole! You're wild, bro! Let's do it!
target: 哇，小斯科特，要来给这洞，一发“骨肉相连”！够野啊，兄弟，走着！

source: Hooray! I'm being included!
target: 好耶！他们肯带我玩了！

source: I rest my case.
target: 看吧，还用我说？

source: Well, you're not proud, but at least your plan worked. The hole owners pay you +N2 MONEY for your consultancy.
target: 不光彩，是不光彩，不过，管用。洞主付给你+N2金钱的咨询费。

source: Soon, bad golfers from all over flock to the hole. They bring golf balls, putters, and backup putters for when they accidentally throw their original putters into the hole.
target: 各地菜鸟高尔夫选手，纷纷赶来，带着球、推杆，还有备用推杆，免得不小心，把原配那根，扔进洞里。

source: Wow, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%. This is SHOCKINGLY boring. Shocking because golf was already so boring, and you somehow made it worse.
target: 哇，%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，无聊到震惊。高尔夫，本来够无聊，你居然还能，让它更无聊。

source: This is weird. Golf is a sport, and it has balls like all the best sports, but even I can't get hyped about this. I'm somehow -N2 HYPE about this.
target: 奇怪。高尔夫是运动，还有好运动都该有的球，可连我，都兴奋不起来。甚至，还-N2热度了。

source: You watch two businessmen approach the bottomless hole. They hit their balls a couple times but can't sink a single put.
target: 两个商人走到无底洞旁，打了几杆，居然一个球，都推不进去。

source: "I sure do love golf!" one says as he hits his ball backwards. "It's so fun, and not tedious or soul-crushing at all!"
target: “真爱高尔夫！”一人，把球打向身后，说道，“多好玩，一点也不枯燥，更不会磨灭灵魂！”

source: "You're right. Golfing is every bit as fun as a meeting that could've been an email."
target: “没错，跟本来一封邮件，就能说清，却非得开的会，一样好玩。”

source: "Wait, do you find that fun?"
target: “等等，你觉得，那好玩？”

source: "...No, actually. I think I've developed a subconscious association between business and golf. Do I only golf for business reasons?"
target: “……其实，不好玩。大概潜意识里，把生意和高尔夫，绑一起了。我打球，只是为了生意？”

source: "I think I do too. Why are we torturing ourselves like this? Why do we have boring business meetings while doing the most boring activity on Earth?"
target: “我好像也是。干吗这样折磨自己？边做世上最无聊的事，边开无聊商务会？”

source: "I have no idea. I think one person suggested it a long time ago -- perhaps ironically -- and we've kept it up out of pure inertia on everyone's part."
target: “谁知道。也许很久以前，有人提了一嘴，搞不好，还是开玩笑。大家就凭惯性，一直这么干了。”

source: "Well I'm tired of it! Let's have our next meeting somewhere actually enjoyable... like a laser tag arena! Or a skatepark!"
target: “反正，我受够了！下次会议，去个真好玩的地方，激光枪战场，或者滑板公园！”

source: Wow, I'm kinda impressed. I didn't think two white-collar business types would be interested in skating or laser tag.
target: 哇，还挺意外。两个白领生意人，居然也爱滑板和激光枪战。

source: "That's just a stereotype. We WORK in business, but we don't live where we work. We still have fun shredding up a skatepark."
target: “刻板印象罢了。工作归工作，又不是住在工作里。滑板场，我们照样玩得飞起。”

source: ...Wanna party with us later?
target: ……晚点，一起派对？

source: And that's the story of how you saved a small business AND pulled a totally rad kickflip on a stockbroker's skateboard in the same day!
target: 就这样，你一天之内，既救了小店，又踩着股票经纪人的滑板，来了个帅到爆的脚尖翻板！

source: And that's the story of how you saved a small business AND snorted coke off a stockbroker's skateboard in the same day!
target: 就这样，你一天之内，既救了小店，又趴在股票经纪人的滑板上，吸了可卡因！

source: The hole owners pay you +N2 MONEY for your consultancy.
target: 洞主付给你+N2金钱的咨询费。

source: Forfeit material goods
target: 舍弃身外之物

source: You tell your friends you'd like to throw some of your most prized possessions into the weird desert hole.
target: 你告诉朋友们，想把最珍贵的几件东西，扔进这个古怪的沙漠洞。

source: Wait, why though? Wouldn't it make more sense to throw your stuff out in a dumpster than a national landmark?
target: 等等，为什么？扔东西，垃圾箱，不比国家地标合适？

source: "You don't know about the ancient traditions?" a random tourist asks. "Throwing one's material possessions into the Great Hole is a hallowed rite!"
target: “不知道古老传统吗？”一位游客问，“向大洞献出身外之物，是神圣仪式！”

source: Whoa, sounds dumb and nonsensical. You have my attention!
target: 哇，听着又蠢、又没道理。我有兴趣了！

source: "Most say the hole is just a tourist trap, but some of us know the truth. The hole is actually the mouth of an ancient deity!"
target: “多半人说，这洞，只是宰游客的。可我们知道真相：洞，其实是古老神明的嘴！”

source: "We throw our material goods into it to appease the deity's timeless hunger. If not for us, it would rise from the desert and consume the universe itself!"
target: “献出财物，才能安抚它永恒的饥饿。没我们，它就会从沙漠起身，把宇宙都吞了！”

source: So you're saving us all from the apocalypse by throwing your old junk in a big hole? That's so selfless of you!
target: 把旧垃圾，扔进大洞，就能救大家，逃过末日？太无私了！

source: "THANK you! If I call my mom right now, would you repeat that back to her?"
target: “谢谢！我现在给妈妈打电话，能再跟她，说一遍吗？”

source: I dunno if I buy all that, but this culty stuff is weird enough to pique my interest. I'll play along.
target: 不一定信，不过，邪教这套，怪得挺有意思，我陪着玩。

source: Here, Hole, take my dad's old pipe. I kept it for sentimental reasons, but my new pipe glows in the dark, and I suspect "glowing in the dark" beats "sentimental value."
target: 洞，收下我爸的旧烟斗。留着，是个念想，可新的，能夜光。想了想，“夜光”，大概比“纪念意义”，强。

source: Good riddance!
target: 扔了好！

source: O Great Hole, here are some of my favorite bones! Normally I'd bury them myself, but I can only dig a good hole, and I heard you're a GREAT hole.
target: 伟大的洞，这是我最爱的几根骨头！平时，我自己埋，可只能挖“好”洞。听说，你是个“伟大”的洞。

source: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%, what're you throwing in the hole?
target: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，你要扔什么？

source: Roll a pair of dice into the hole... AND NEVER KNOW WHAT NUMBER YOU ROLLED.

source: "Snakes do NOT make healthy romantic partners. They'll get you in their vice grip, then suddenly you're backsliding into the pits of their hungry mouths!"
target: “蛇可不是健康的恋爱对象。他们先把你缠得死死的，然后你一滑，就掉进他们那张饥肠辘辘的大嘴里了！”

source: "I can build you a ladder to get out of that pit. But it's much better if I TEACH you how to build your own metaphorical ladder."
target: “我可以给你们搭个梯子，爬出这个坑。不过更好的办法，是教你们亲手搭起这架比喻意义上的梯子。”

source: Yeah, but I had like five shots of vodka before we got here, and Scott is... Scott. Good luck teaching us ANYTHING right now.
target: 话是这么说，可我来之前喝了大概五杯伏特加，斯科特嘛……他是斯科特。想让我们现在学进去点什么？祝你好运。

source: Yeah, but I did like three tabs of acid before we got here, and Scott is... Scott. Good luck teaching us ANYTHING right now.
target: 话是这么说，可我来之前吃了大概三片 LSD，斯科特嘛……他是斯科特。想让我们现在学进去点什么？祝你好运。

source: Dr. Mongoose pinches his adorable little snoot exasperatedly. "Ugh, fine. Looks like it's time for plan B."
target: 猫鼬医生无奈地捏了捏自己可爱的小鼻子。“唉，好吧。看来得上 B 计划了。”

source: He starts swatting Scott and Polly with a rolled-up newspaper.
target: 他卷起一份报纸，开始抽打斯科特和波莉。

source: "SNAKES ARE BAD! SNAKES = BAD! ASSOCIATE THIS PAIN WITH SNAKES, BOTH OF WHICH ARE BAD!"
target: “蛇不好！蛇＝坏东西！把这种痛和蛇联系起来！两样都不好！”

source: OW! Stop swatting me, Dr. Mongoose! I didn't even pee on the carpet or anything!
target: 嗷！别打我了，猫鼬医生！我又没往地毯上撒尿！

source: The newspaper therapy fails to take hold, so Dr. Mongoose finally resorts to plan C, which is apparently just eating the snakes.
target: 报纸疗法没起作用，猫鼬医生只好使出 C 计划。看起来，这计划就是直接把蛇吃了。

source: NOOOOO, SSSSAMUEL! He promised to take me to see Pompeii...
target: 不——！嘶……塞缪尔！他答应带我去看庞贝古城的……

source: "His promises were empty, unlike my belly!" laughs Dr. Mongoose. "You're cured! My methods never fail -- especially my method of just eating the snakes."
target: “他的承诺是空的，我的肚子可不空！”猫鼬医生大笑着说，“你们治好了！我的疗法从不失手——尤其是直接吃蛇这一招。”

source: Don't worry, %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%: once Polly and Scott stop crying over their boyfriends' deaths, they'll see how right you were.
target: 别担心，%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%。等波莉和斯科特不再为男友的死哭哭啼啼，就会明白你有多正确。

source: It may have been a long, boring, -N2 HYPE way of doing it, but you gain +N2 SOUL for saving your friends all the same!
target: 虽然这个办法又慢又无聊，让你失去了 -N2 热度，但救下朋友还是让你获得了 +N2 灵魂！

source: Soon, you're all aboard Sailor Shrimp's Barge to Augusta, Maine.
target: 很快，你们全上了开往缅因州奥古斯塔的“虾水手号驳船”。

source: It's hot, it's noisy, it's full of bitchy tourists, and it's expensive! The perfect breakup cocktail!
target: 船上又热又吵，游客个个爱找茬，票价还死贵！完美的分手套餐！

source: So this is a cruise, huh? Aren't these things supposed to be... fun?
target: 这就是游轮旅行啊？这种旅行不是应该……挺好玩吗？

source: "Ahoy, passengers!" says a man in a cheesy calamari costume. "I'm Sailor Shrimp, your happy cruise guide! Who's ready for shuffleboard?"
target: “啊嗬，乘客们！”一个穿着廉价鱿鱼戏服的男人说，“我是虾水手，各位的快乐游轮导游！谁准备好玩沙狐球啦？”

source: Kill me. Kill me again. Bring me back to life, and kill me again. I'd rather do that than play shuffleboard.
target: 杀了我吧。再杀一遍。先把我复活，再杀一遍。我宁可这样也不想玩沙狐球。

source: "Cheer up, buttercup! There's TONS of activities aboard Sailor Shrimp's Barge! We've got karaoke, Trivial Pursuit, swimming in a crowded pool mere feet from the ocean..."
target: “开心点嘛，小可爱！虾水手号上的活动多着呢！卡拉 OK、《Trivial Pursuit》问答桌游，还有在离大海几步远的拥挤泳池里游泳……”

source: The only activity I'm interested in is the bar. Let's go.
target: 我唯一感兴趣的活动就是去酒吧。走吧。

source: Polly, I've been meaning to talk to you about your drinking. I'm worried it'ssss bad for your health, and alsssso I don't like to eat a fatty liver.
target: 嘶……波莉，我一直想跟你聊聊喝酒的事。我担心这对你的健康不好，再说，我也不爱吃脂肪肝。

source: Ugh, I am DONE with you telling me what to drink, what to eat, and to practice fitting my head in your unhinged jaw! When do we get to do something I wanna do?!
target: 烦死了！你一会儿管我喝什么，一会儿管我吃什么，还让我练习把脑袋塞进你那张大嘴里！到底什么时候才能干点我想干的事？！

source: "Ahoy, it's Sailor Shrimp here again! I need to, uh, assign you this screaming child."
target: “啊嗬，虾水手又来啦！我得，呃，把这个尖叫的小孩分给你们照看。”

source: "The deck's full of them, we don't know whose is whose, and they keep falling overboard. Can you make sure this one doesn't die? Awesome sauce!"
target: “甲板上到处都是小孩，谁是谁家的我们也搞不清，而且他们老往海里掉。能保证这个别死掉吗？棒极了！”

source: Sure. Hey, little bro! Wanna see how many erasers I can stuff up my nose?
target: 没问题。嘿，小老弟！想看我鼻孔里能塞几块橡皮吗？

source: You're not sssseriously keeping the little crotch goblin, are you? Let'ssss just eat him!
target: 嘶……你不会真打算留着这小屁孩吧？直接吃了不就好了！

source: No way! I admit I may have been misleading on my stance on eating people throughout our relationship, but only Wolf Scott is into that.
target: 不行！我承认，谈恋爱的时候，我对吃人这事的态度可能让你误会了。但只有狼形态的斯科特才爱吃人。

source: Me Scott loves kids! I want some of my own someday! Do you... not want that?
target: 现在这个斯科特喜欢小孩！我以后还想有自己的孩子呢！你……不想要吗？

source: "Ahoy again!" says Sailor Shrimp, king of not reading the room. "Ready for your mandatory Sailor Shrimp Barge family photo? Saaaaay SHELLFISH!"
target: “啊嗬，又见面了！”虾水手说道。这位真是一点也不会看气氛。“准备好拍虾水手号的强制全家福了吗？一起喊——贝——壳！”

source: Your friends break up with their snake boyfriends and swim back to shore that night! You gain +N2 SOUL for saving them, but lost -N2 MONEY buying cruise tickets.
target: 那天晚上，朋友们就跟蛇男友分了手，游回岸上去了！救下他们让你获得 +N2 灵魂，但买游轮票也花掉了 -N2 金钱。

source: Improv iguanas
target: 鬣蜥即兴喜剧

source: You settle in to watch the pinnacle of modern entertainment: low-budget improv comedy! Three iguanas come out onstage.
target: 你坐下来欣赏现代娱乐的巅峰：低成本即兴喜剧！三只鬣蜥走上舞台。

source: Welcome to the show, guys! We're gonna start by drawing a scene from a hat. That scene is... pirate ship!
target: 欢迎大家来看演出！先从帽子里抽个场景。我们抽到的是……海盗船！

source: (Irving! That's not the scene we practiced. You were supposed to draw the romcom scene!)
target: （欧文！这不是咱们排练过的场景。你应该抽到浪漫喜剧的！）

source: (Oh, no, you're right! I really messed up... guess we'll just have to wing our improv!)
target: （糟了，你说得对！我搞砸了……看来这场即兴表演，只能临场发挥了！）

source: Oh, Lord.
target: 老天啊。

source: ARRRR, we sure are on a pirate ship right now! I'm the pirate captain. You can tell by my accent and my hand covering my eye in place of an eyepatch!
target: 啊哈！咱们现在就在海盗船上！我是海盗船长，听这口音就知道了。我还拿手捂着一只眼睛，当眼罩用！

source: How is a hand an eyepatch? I don't understand this scene at all.
target: 手怎么能当眼罩？这场戏我完全看不懂。

source: Oh no, Irving -- er, uh, Pirate Irving! There's a storm coming!
target: 不好啦，欧文——呃，海盗欧文！暴风雨要来了！

source: No there's not. It's a clear, sunny day!
target: 才没有。今天晴空万里，阳光明媚！

source: (IRVING! Why aren't you "yes, and"-ing me?!)
target: （欧文！你怎么不按“对，而且……”的原则接我的戏？！）

source: (Oh, right!) Uh, I mean, it's a clear sunny day, YES AND there's a storm coming!
target: （哦，对！）呃，我是说，今天晴空万里，阳光明媚，对，而且暴风雨要来了！

source: Aaaand scene!
Thanks for the applause, Mom! Now we're taking audience requests! Pitch a scene, any scene, and we'll create it with the power of improv!
target: 谢谢你的掌声，妈妈！现在请观众出题！随便说一个场景，我们都能靠即兴表演演出来！

source: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%, go suggest something entertaining please. I'm LITERALLY dying of -N2 HYPE-itis right now.
target: %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%，求你快提个有意思的题目吧。我真的快被“热度 -N2 炎”给无聊死了。

source: Yikes, that shit's contagious. What do you pitch to the improv iguanas to save the show?
target: 坏了，这病还会传染。你要给这群即兴鬣蜥出什么题，才能挽救这场演出？

source: The scene is a group of very good improv actors who feel truly beloved by their audience, realized in their careers, and finally accepted by their emotionally distant parents.
target: 场景是：一群优秀的即兴演员，深受观众喜爱、事业有成，终于得到了不善表达感情的父母的认可。

source: The scene is a group of iguana actors in a dystopian future where actors pay their audience.
target: 场景是：一群鬣蜥演员生活在反乌托邦的未来，演员得付钱给观众。

source: Okay, we can do that! *Ahem!* Hey, Good Actor Irving! What are you doing today?
target: 好，这个我们会演！咳咳！嘿，优秀演员欧文！今天在忙什么？

source: Not much, just reheating some three-day-old ramen because I can't afford groceries again, haha!
target: 没什么，又买不起菜了，正在热三天前剩下的拉面，哈哈！

source: Don't give up, Irving. The world may not appreciate you yet, but you ARE a good actor. Get out there tonight and show 'em who's boss!
target: 别灰心，欧文。也许世人还不懂欣赏你，可你真的是个好演员。今晚就上台，让他们见识见识！

source: Irving then takes the stage and starts "performing" as a "good actor." He's telling the worst jokes you've ever heard, but at least he seems more confident about it!
target: 接着，欧文走上台，开始“扮演”一位“优秀演员”。他讲的笑话难听得前所未有，不过至少看着更有自信了！

source: You're amazing, Good Actor Irving! Look around, the crowd loves you!
target: 你太棒了，优秀演员欧文！看看周围，观众都爱你！

source: Woohoo! Go Irving!
target: 呜呼！欧文，加油！

source: (Whoa, do you hear that cheering? Good Actor Irving is really good at this acting thing!)
target: （哇，听到欢呼声了吗？优秀演员欧文还真挺会演戏的！）

source: Irving! It's me, your emotionally distant father. I saw your performance last night -- you were great!
target: 欧文！是我，你那个不善表达感情的爸爸。我看了你昨晚的表演，真棒！

source: Oh! Uhh, thanks, Dad! (Wow, I had no idea our improv troupe got more members...)
target: 哦！呃，谢谢爸爸！（哇，咱们即兴剧团什么时候又招新人了……）

source: Son, to be honest, I always thought improv was super lame. I mean, who doesn't? It's very, very lame.
target: 儿子，说实话，我以前一直觉得即兴表演特别逊。谁不这么想呢？真的，特别特别逊。

source: But today, you proved me wrong. Improv is only a little lame. I'm proud of you for not being very, very lame. I love you, kiddo.
target: 不过今天，你证明我错了。即兴表演也就有一点逊。你没有特别特别逊，我为你骄傲。我爱你，孩子。

source: Oh, Dad! You don't know how much that means to me!
target: 哦，爸爸！你不知道这话对我有多重要！

source: Irving starts to cry real tears (he is NOT a good enough actor to fake that). This was the therapy session he always needed but could never afford. You gain +N2 SOUL!
target: 欧文真的哭了出来（他的演技还不足以装得这么真）。他一直需要心理治疗，却始终付不起钱，今天总算补上了。你获得 +N2 灵魂！

source: Okay... *ahem!* Oh no, Robot Irving! In the distant future, all of our brains have been implanted in robot bodies!
target: 好……咳咳！不好了，机器人欧文！在遥远的未来，我们所有人的大脑都被装进了机器人身体里！

source: Oh, no! How can we, impassioned players of the improvised stage, still entertain our audience with these emotionless, mechanical bodies?
target: 糟了！我们这些对即兴舞台满怀热情的演员，要怎么用这副冷冰冰、毫无感情的机械身体，继续取悦观众呢？

source: I've got it! Let's PAY our audience to like us! I'm beaming the audience 100 Robobucks from my mind. HRRRRGHGGKGKKHGH!
target: 有了！花钱让观众喜欢我们！我正用意念给观众传送一百机器币。哼啊啊咯咯咯啊！

source: Is the iguana trying to pay us, or is he really constipated?
target: 那只鬣蜥是想给我们钱，还是便秘得太厉害了？

source: I'm not convinced. I went to see a gecko improv show last week, and they used REAL props -- including a real gun for the tragic death scene! Now that's commitment.
target: 没说服力。我上周看了场壁虎即兴喜剧，人家可都用真道具——悲剧死亡场面甚至用了真枪！这才叫敬业。

source: Hey, we're committed! Um, we have... four dollars and thirty-eight cents between us.
target: 嘿，我们也很敬业！呃，我们几个凑起来……有四块三毛八。

source: It was our bus fare to get home, but we'll walk if it's for the noble art of theater!
target: 那是我们回家的公交车费，不过为了崇高的戏剧艺术，走回去也行！

source: Come on, you can do better than that! This is IMPROV, people! If you don't have enough money to pay us, you gotta IMPROVISE a way to get some money!
target: 拿出点本事来啊！各位，这可是即兴表演！没钱付给观众，那就即兴想个办法搞点钱！

source: I've got an idea. Just go to a bank! Banks have money! Improv the bank into giving you money!
target: 我有个主意，去银行啊！银行有钱！即兴演到银行肯给你们钱不就好了！

source: Scott coming in clutch with the suggestions! The improv iguanas break into a bank wearing robot masks.
target: 斯科特这主意真是关键！即兴鬣蜥们戴上机器人面具，闯进了银行。

source: This is a stickup... FROM THE FUTURE! Give us all your money, or we'll shoot you with these super real ray-guns in our pockets!
target: 这是抢劫……来自未来的抢劫！把钱全交出来，不然就用我们口袋里这几把绝对是真的射线枪打你们！

source: (Wow, Irving, they're actually giving us the money! We're, like, the most convincing actors ever!)
target: （哇，欧文，他们真的在给我们钱！我们简直是史上最有说服力的演员！）

source: The iguanas distribute the money to the audience amidst roaring applause. Their utter joy is priceless, especially knowing they won't be nearly so joyful when they're arrested.
target: 鬣蜥们在雷鸣般的掌声中，把钱分给了观众。他们喜不自胜的样子真是无价之宝，尤其想到等被逮捕时，他们可就开心不起来了。

source: But who cares about them, this is about YOU! And you just got +N2 MONEY!
target: 不过谁管他们啊，这故事说的是你！而你刚赚了 +N2 金钱！

source: A crocodile, but it's a stage magician
target: 一条鳄鱼，但职业是舞台魔术师

source: You settle in to watch the show. The stagehands bring out a stool, a microphone, and a 1,100-pound reptilian killing machine in a funny hat.
target: 你坐下来准备看演出。工作人员搬来一张凳子、一个麦克风，还有一头戴着滑稽帽子、重达一千一百磅的爬行动物杀戮机器。

source: I am Reptilizar, famed crocodilian magician, known far and wide throughout the Everglades! Prepare to be amazed!
target: 我就是名扬整个大沼泽地的鳄鱼魔术大师，雷普蒂利扎！准备大开眼界吧！

source: For my first trick, I will make this rabbit disappear!
target: 第一个魔术，我要让这只兔子消失！

source: Someone brings the croc a rabbit. He puts his hat in front of his face. The bunny shrieks, then there's chewing sounds.
target: 有人把兔子递给鳄鱼。他拿帽子挡住脸。兔子一声惨叫，接着传来咀嚼声。

source: Okay, you're obviously just eating the rabbit. You can't call the food chain "magic", boo.
target: 你明明就是把兔子吃了。亲爱的，不能把食物链叫作“魔法”吧。

source: Hmph! I see we've got some hecklers in tonight's audience! You doubt now, but wait until you see my next trick...
target: 哼！看来今晚的观众里有人爱拆台！现在尽管怀疑，等你看到我的下一个魔术……

source: I'll make this ENTIRE PIG disappear over the course of an hour, with the aid of this magical BBQ sauce!
target: 在这瓶魔法烧烤酱的帮助下，我要用一个小时，让这整头猪消失！

source: You're not even trying. Can't you make anything disappear without just eating it?
target: 你根本都懒得装了吧。除了吃，能不能用别的办法让东西消失？

source: UGH! Of course I can! Reptilizar can make ANYTHING disappear! Anything you can think of, I'll make it gone!
target: 啧！当然可以！雷普蒂利扎能让任何东西消失！随便说一样，我都能把它变没！

source: Say, if he's telling the truth, that could be really useful. And if he's lying, it's all the more entertaining for you! What do you ask the croc to make disappear?
target: 诶，要是他说的是真的，那可太实用了。要是吹牛呢，你也能看个更大的乐子！你要让这条鳄鱼变没什么东西？

source: "All of my adult obligations!"
target: “我作为成年人的一切责任！”

source: "My internet search history, because of... reasons."
target: “我的网络搜索记录。因为……某些原因。”

source: Adult obligations? You mean, like, wearing underwear?
target: 成年人的责任？你是说，像穿内裤这种？

source: Nah, I want the whole shebang: no more work, no more meetings, just time to sit around and play video games!
target: 不，我要一整套：不用工作，不用开会，整天坐着打游戏就行！

source: Very well... SHIBBY SHOOBY ALAKAZOOEY!
target: 好……西比舒比阿拉卡祖伊！

source: Reptilizar waves a magic wand around... then grabs your phone out of your lap before you can stop him.
target: 雷普蒂利扎挥了挥魔杖……然后趁你没来得及阻止，一把抢走了你放在腿上的手机。

source: Hello, is this %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%'s boss? ...Great!
target: 喂，您好，是%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%的老板吗？……太好了！

source: I'm calling on behalf of %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%; %HESHE% %VERB_IS_ARE% quitting %HISHER% job, effective immediately.
target: 我是替%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%打来的。%HESHE%%VERB_IS_ARE%要辞掉%HISHER%工作，立即生效。
notes: pending review 109 (2026-10-22): POLISH; 鳄鱼替玩家辞职；中文要辞掉足以表达进行体。 按行中文动词展开已实现；未实机验证。

source: WHAT?!
target: 什么？！

source: Yes, %HESHE%%VERB_'S_'RE% absolutely serious. And to really burn the bridge, %HESHE% would like you to know -- and I am quoting %HIMHER% directly here...
target: 没错，%HESHE%%VERB_'S_'RE%认真的。为了彻底撕破脸，%HESHE%还想让您知道——我直接引用%HIMHER%的原话……
notes: pending review 109 (2026-10-22): KEEP; 鳄鱼强调辞职认真并焚桥；展开为是，组成是认真的。 按行中文动词展开已实现；未实机验证。

source: That you are an "incompetent, insufferable poopy-head whose only positive contribution to the world would be dropping dead."
target: 您就是个“无能又讨人嫌的屎脑袋，对世界唯一能做的好事，就是赶紧去死”。

source: FUCK YEAH, GO OFF!
target: 操，对，就这么骂！

source: Pitch your business ideas to investors
target: 向投资人推介商业点子

source: A panel of "high-profile investors" have gathered at the summit to hear business ideas. You and your friends are next in line to present.
target: 一群“知名投资人”齐聚峰会，听取创业提案。下一个就轮到你和朋友们上场。

source: Ugh, why did I agree to do this off-brand "Shark Tank" shit? If I hear one more pyramid scheme pitch, my hair's going to eat its own tail.
target: 唉，我干吗答应来搞这种山寨《Shark Tank》的破玩意？再听一个传销项目，我的头发都要开始咬自己的尾巴了。

source: I'm starting to think this isn't one of those game shows where one of the contestants falls in love with me at the end...
target: 我开始觉得，这好像不是那种节目结束时，就会有一位选手爱上我的综艺……

source: Why has nobody pitched anything I can put in a shopping mall?! The wheels of commerce are turning in all the wrong directions!
target: 怎么就没人提一个能放进购物中心的点子？！商业的齿轮全在往错误的方向转！

source: HELLOOOO, POTENTIAL INVESTORS! I'm Polly Geist, the President of Prank Masterz, Inc.!
target: 各位潜在投资人，大家好——！我是恶作剧大师公司总裁，波莉·鬼斯特！

source: And I'm Scott Howl, professional good boy!
target: 我是斯科特·嚎尔，职业好狗狗！

source: Let's set the scene: you're a rich investor who has it all: loads of money, a plot of land on Mars, and probably a robo-butler.
target: 想象一下：你是个什么都有的富豪投资人。有花不完的钱，在火星有块地，可能还有个机器人管家。

source: Your life is just missing one thing: fun!
target: 你的生活就缺一样东西：乐趣！

source: That's why the Prank Masterz are now offering a monthly subscription service where we come to your house and prank you!
target: 所以，恶作剧大师现在推出包月服务，上门给你搞恶作剧！

source: If you invest 100,000 dollars, you'll get a 10% share of our company, and we'll even throw in these microwave burritos we found in Scott's pocket!
target: 投资十万美元，就能拿到我们公司百分之十的股份！还附赠从斯科特口袋里翻出来的这些微波墨西哥卷饼！

source: I love you guys, but -- and I mean no disrespect -- this idea of yours sound very dumb.
target: 我很喜欢你们，不过——没有冒犯的意思——你们这点子听着真的很蠢。

source: I do have a robo-butler... so these two youngsters might be onto something here...
target: 我确实有个机器人管家……所以这两个年轻人，可能还真有点想法……

source: I am intrigued. An idea being very dumb has never stopped a billionaire from making more millions...
target: 我很感兴趣。点子蠢，从来也没耽误亿万富翁再赚几百万……

source: Exactly! It already happened with robo-butlers. What if "pranks" are the new "robo-butlers"?
target: 没错！机器人管家就是先例。万一“恶作剧”就是下一个“机器人管家”呢？

source: These investors (minus Vera) seem on the verge of giving you money for your (clearly dumb) idea. Push them in the right direction with your business pitch skills!
target: 除了薇拉，这些投资人眼看就要为你那显然很蠢的点子掏钱了。发挥你的推介技巧，推他们一把！

source: A business idea gains power when it's backed by experts, and you have the trust of the best expert out there. Tell them your mom says this is a good idea.
target: 有专家背书，商业点子就更有说服力。而最权威的专家正好支持你：告诉他们，你妈妈说这是个好点子。

source: Investors appreciate a good deal. Give them a referral code. If they bring 3 more investors to the deal, they get a free hot dog with their equity.
target: 投资人最爱划算的买卖。给他们一个推荐码，再拉来三位投资人，就能在股份之外，额外领到一根免费热狗。

source: Really? Then I'm in!
target: 真的？那我投！

source: I follow %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%'s mom on her socials, and I trust her wholeheartedly.
target: 我关注了%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%妈妈的社交账号，我对她绝对信任。

source: You follow...? WHY?
target: 你关注了……为什么？

source: I don't know... it just seemed like a creepy thing to do, and that's kind of my brand, I guess.
target: 不知道……感觉这事挺变态的，算是我的个人风格吧。

source: Ooh, let me see. Show me %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%'s mom's profile.
target: 哦，让我看看。给我看看%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%妈妈的主页。

source: ...What? No! Why is everyone following your mom now? What have you done?!
target: ……什么？别啊！怎么大家都关注你妈去了？你都干了些什么？！

source: Look, she always shares these memes with the little yellow creature in overalls. It's pretty funny! Hard not to trust this woman!
target: 你看，她老转发那个穿背带裤的黄色小家伙的表情包。还挺好笑的！很难不信任这样的女士！

source: It is funny! Is she single?
target: 确实好笑！她单身吗？

source: For fuck's sake, can you two PLEASE stop stalking %CURRENTPLAYERNAME%'s mom?!
target: 操，你们两个能不能别再窥探%CURRENTPLAYERNAME%妈妈的生活了？！

source: I would also appreciate that, honestly.
target: 说真的，我也求你们了。

source: Look, I still think this is dumb, but I was tired of doing this investment event hours ago and I just want this to be over.
target: 听着，我还是觉得这点子很蠢。不过这场投资活动我几个小时前就受够了，现在只想赶紧结束。

source: If I "invest" twenty bucks, will you just leave me alone for the rest of the day?
target: 我“投资”二十块，你们今天剩下的时间能不能别来烦我？

source: Do we get to keep the burritos?
target: 卷饼我们还能留着吗？

source: ...Yes.
Vera Oberlin: you've got a deal!
target: 薇拉·奥伯林，成交！

source: Vera gives you +N2 MONEY, but you do lose -N2 HYPE for trying to look cool by mentioning your mom likes you.
target: 薇拉给了你 +N2 金钱，但你搬出“我妈喜欢我”来装酷，也让你失去了 -N2 热度。

source: You want us to invest 100,000 dollars AND find three more investors, only for a hot dog?!
target: 你们想让我们投十万美元，再找三个投资人，就为了根热狗？！

source: We could just buy a hot dog with those 100,000 dollars, you idiots.
target: 蠢货，我们直接拿这十万美元买根热狗不就行了？

source: ...Could we? I have no idea how much a hot dog costs.
target: ……行吗？我完全不知道一根热狗多少钱。

source: Uhm, it surely costs something under 100,000... I think.
target: 呃，肯定不到十万吧……我觉得。

source: (Are you totally sure? We could be passing up on a good deal here).
target: （你确定吗？咱们可能会错过一笔好买卖。）

source: (Fuck, you could be right... ugh... being an investor is so hard sometimes...)
target: （操，说不定你是对的……唉……当投资人有时候真难……）

source: (It's okay, don't sweat it. Let me lead on this, okay?)
target: （没事，别紧张。我来谈，好吗？）

source: Listen you three, my friend here and I are interested in joining forces:
target: 你们三个听着，我和这位朋友有意联手：

source: We will co-invest in your venture with 250,000 dollars, but we want 25% and one hot dog each.
target: 我们共同投资二十五万美元，要百分之二十五的股份，另外每人一根热狗。

source: Twenty dollars and you get 15% and half a hot dog, final offer!
target: 二十美元，给你们百分之十五的股份，再加半根热狗，最终报价！

source: SCOTT, NO!
target: 斯科特，别！

source: Deal!
target: 说定了!

source: WHYYYYYYYY?!
target: 为什么啊——？！

source: (Polly, it was the only way. I ate half the hot dog while they were whispering. You gotta trust me on this one.)
target: （波莉，只能这样了。他们说悄悄话的时候，我已经吃了半根热狗。这次你得相信我。）

source: Ha! We did it, partner!
target: 哈！搭档，咱们成功了！

source: How do you morons even dress yourselves in the mornings?
target: 你们这帮蠢货，早上到底怎么自己穿好衣服的？

source: I don't! I have an intern for that!
target: 我不自己穿啊！我有实习生干这个！

source: I'm out.
target: 我走了。

source: Woohoo, you did it! You get +20 DOLLARS, which at the current exchange rate is equivalent to +N2 MONEY. But you lost -N2 STAMINA giving away your (half of a) hot dog.
target: 呜呼，成了！你赚到 +20 美元，按当前汇率，相当于 +N2 金钱。但送出了自己的（半根）热狗，让你失去了 -N2 体力。

source: Fight the kaiju
target: 对抗巨兽

source: One convenient scene transition later, you're suddenly in city hall debating on how to fight the kaiju.
target: 一次方便省事的转场后，你们突然就到了市政厅，开始商量怎么对付巨兽。

source: "I've gathered the city's greatest minds -- and these random tourists for some reason -- to discuss solutions," says the mayor. "What can we do?"
target: “我召集了全市最聪明的人——还有这几个不知为何在场的游客——来讨论解决方案。”市长说，“各位有什么办法？”

source: "Let's use bombs!" the military general says. "We're flush with nukes! This kaiju is just the excuse we need to blow shit up again!"
target: “用炸弹！”军方将领说，“我们核弹多得是！正愁没借口再炸点什么呢，这巨兽来得正好！”

source: I like this guy. I like his whole unhinged vibe.
target: 我喜欢这家伙，喜欢他这股彻底疯掉的劲儿。

source: "Let's, uh, put a pin in that," says the mayor. "Scientists, do you have any ideas? Where did the kaiju come from?"
target: “呃，这个先放一放。”市长说，“科学家们，有什么想法？这巨兽是从哪儿来的？”

source: "Well," say the scientists, "it's possible that all the untreated radioactive waste in the water supply mutated a lizard into a giant killing machine."
target: “嗯，”科学家们说，“可能是供水系统里那些没处理的放射性废料，让一只蜥蜴变成了巨型杀戮机器。”

source: "Damn, if it isn't the consequences of my own actions," sighs the mayor. "Just tell me how to kill the damn thing!"
target: “该死，原来这就是我自作自受的后果。”市长叹气，“直接告诉我怎么弄死它吧！”

source: "Kill the kaiju?" gasp the scientists. "Why would you want to do that? Kaijus are awesome!"
target: “弄死巨兽？”科学家们倒吸一口气，“为什么要这样？巨兽超酷的！”

source: Ooh, you know what would work? Fighting fire with fire. Let's sic another kaiju on the first kaiju to kill it!
target: 哦，我知道怎么办！以毒攻毒。再弄一头巨兽来，干掉这头巨兽！

source: "Won't that cause undue harm to the civilians?" the mayor sighs. "Does anyone here have an idea that WON'T kill thousands of innocents?"
target: “这不会殃及平民吗？”市长叹气，“在座就没人能想个不会害死成千上万无辜市民的办法？”

source: Have you tried offering the kaiju a free pizza if it promises not to stomp on anyone?
target: 你们试过送巨兽一个免费披萨，让它保证不踩人了吗？

source: "...Okay, looks like the kaiju vs. kaiju thing is our best bet. But where are we going to find ANOTHER kaiju to sic on the first one?"
target: “……行吧，看来让巨兽打巨兽是最靠谱的办法。可上哪儿再找一头巨兽，来对付这头呢？”

source: Hey, for some reason, you know exactly where! You just need to...
target: 嘿，不知道为什么，你正好知道！你们只需要……

source: Call Hypperion, the Hungry Hungry Hippo of Hyper-Hope.
target: 召唤超希望岛的饿饿河马，河珀里翁（Hypperion）。

source: Bring a skyscraper to life so the buildings can get their revenge after decades of the kaijus' tyranny!
target: 赋予摩天大楼生命，让建筑们有机会报复横行霸道了几十年的巨兽！

source: "HYPPERION?!" the scientists gasp. "But that's just a legend! Nobody even knows if it exists!"
target: “河珀里翁？！”科学家们惊呼，“那只是个传说！连它到底存不存在都没人知道！”

source: But we're in movie-logic territory right now. Everyone knows that if a movie character says something's just a legend, it's usually true. Time for a hippo hunt!
target: 可我们现在是按电影逻辑走的。谁都知道，电影里有人说“那只是个传说”，那八成就是真的。找河马去！

source: Your search takes you to Hyper-Hope Island, where it's said that Hypperion and other giant hippos have battled for centuries to consume the most balls.
target: 你们一路找到超希望岛。据说，河珀里翁和其他巨型河马为了抢着吃到最多的球，已经争斗了几个世纪。

source: (Don't ask me why they fight over and eat balls. Ancient legends are fucking weird.)
target: （别问我它们为什么非得抢球吃。远古传说就是他妈的怪。）

source: In the end, Hypperion finds you first. It towers over you, blotting out the sun, and booms:
target: 最后，还是河珀里翁先找到了你们。它高耸入云，遮天蔽日，声音如雷：

source: DO YOU HAVE ANY BAAAAAAAAALLS?
target: 你们有没——有——蛋——啊？

source: Yeah, I've got two of 'em! ...Wait, you're not gonna eat them, are you?
target: 有啊，我有两个！……等等，你不会想吃吧？

source: You all lure Hypperion back to the city with the promise of many balls to eat. The kaiju and Hypperion size each other up.
target: 你们答应有大把的球给它吃，把河珀里翁引回了城里。它和巨兽互相打量着。

source: GIVE ME YOUR BALLS!
target: 把你的蛋交出来！

source: "MAKE ME!" says the kaiju. Hypperion tackles the kaiju!
target: “有本事来拿啊！”巨兽说。河珀里翁扑了上去！

source: An action-packed battle ensues. It would cost, like, triple this game's budget to show it to you, so you'll just have to trust me when I say it's very, very awesome.
target: 一场惊险刺激的大战爆发了。真拍给你看，大概要花掉这游戏三倍的预算。所以相信我就好：真的特别、特别酷。

source: At the most dire moment, it seems Hypperion is beat. It falls on its back, perhaps never to rise again, and cries out...
target: 最危急的时刻，河珀里翁似乎落败了。它仰面倒下，也许再也站不起来，仰天喊道……

source: BRETHREN! I CALL UPON YOUR STRENGTH! FEAST UPON THESE BAAAAAAAAALLS!
target: 同胞们！请助我一臂之力！来吃这些蛋——吧！

source: The ground shakes as three more giant hippos come out of the sea! They're the hungry hippos Hypperion eternally fought, come together to defeat a greater foe!
target: 大地震颤，又有三头巨型河马从海里走了出来！正是那些和河珀里翁争斗不休的饿饿河马，如今为了更强的敌人联手了！

source: The hippos form up like Voltron to kill the kaiju. It fucking rules.
target: 河马们像 Voltron 一样合体，干掉了巨兽。简直他妈的帅炸。

source: Afterwards, the hippos feast on the kaiju's balls, but they're still hungry afterwards!
target: 战后，河马们大吃了一顿巨兽的蛋蛋，可吃完还是饿！

source: You satisfy their appetites by playing a giant game of Hungry Hungry Hippos. It's hella fun, and you gain +N2 HYPE!
target: 你们玩起了巨型版《饿饿河马》，总算让它们吃饱了。好玩得要命，你获得 +N2 热度！

source: But you lose -N2 STAMINA because it takes a LOT of giant, balled-up food to appease the hippos.
target: 不过你也失去 -N2 体力，毕竟要喂饱这些河马，得准备海量揉成巨型球状的食物。

source: "BRILLIANT!" the scientists cry. "Kaijus have destroyed cities for eons, and cities are made of buildings. So the buildings have probably built up resentment against kaijus!"
target: “妙啊！”科学家们喊道，“巨兽毁坏城市这么久，城市又都是建筑组成的。建筑肯定早就攒了一肚子对巨兽的怨气！”

source: "Unfortunately, science isn't at the point where we can bring a whole building to life... but magic is! BRING OUT DR. WIZARD!"
target: “可惜，科学还没发展到能让整栋楼活过来的地步……但魔法可以！请巫师博士出场！”

source: Dr. Wizard exerts -N2 MAGIC bringing a skyscraper to life! (It so happens to be your MAGIC because you suggested it... deal with it.)
target: 巫师博士消耗 -N2 魔力，让一栋摩天大楼活了过来！（花的正好是你的魔力，谁让主意是你出的……认了吧。）

source: I... I'm alive? I have... thoughts? A voice? A unique sense of self? This is horrifying!
target: 我……我活了？我有了……思想？声音？独立的自我意识？太可怕了！

source: Welcome to the burden of consciousness, bro! Do you feel like fighting a kaiju?
target: 兄弟，欢迎背上意识的重担！想不想跟巨兽打一架？

source: A kaiju? What is a kaiju? What is a bro? What are all of these words and associations I don't have?!
target: 巨兽？巨兽是什么？兄弟又是什么？这些词是什么意思，彼此又有什么关系，我怎么都不知道？！

source: Ugh, it's like talking to a brick wall -- pun intended but not enjoyed. SOMETHING'S gotta kill this ugly lizard monster...
target: 唉，真是跟堵砖墙说话——对，我故意玩的双关，但一点也不好笑。总得有什么东西能干掉这丑蜥蜴怪吧……

source: Wait, did you say "ugly lizard monster?" I've seen one... it killed my father. If that horrible thing is threatening us again, I will fight!
target: 等等，你刚说“丑蜥蜴怪”？我见过一只……它杀了我父亲。如果那可怕的东西又来威胁我们，我会战斗！

source: Buildings have parents? How do buildings fuck?! Who knows; at least the skyscraper is inspired to fight the kaiju now!
target: 建筑还有父母？建筑他妈的怎么上床？！谁知道呢，反正这栋摩天大楼总算有动力打巨兽了！

source: An action-packed, cinematic battle ensues. It would cost, like, triple this game's budget to show it to you, so you'll just have to trust me when I say it's very, very awesome.
target: 一场电影般惊险刺激的大战爆发了。真拍给你看，大概要花掉这游戏三倍的预算。所以相信我就好：真的特别、特别酷。

source: At the most dire moment, the skyscraper is a half-crumbled mess. All hope seems lost... until it has a flashback to the day it was built!
target: 最危急的时刻，摩天大楼已经塌了一半。眼看大势已去……它却突然回忆起自己建成的那一天！

source: During construction, the foreman asked the architect, "Why are we adding a giant flamethrower to the top 5 stories, Mr. Hanson? Isn't that a huge waste of space?"
target: 施工时，工头曾问建筑师：“汉森先生，为什么要在最上面五层装个巨型火焰喷射器？这不是太浪费空间了吗？”

source: "Ah, young foreman... an architect never reveals the complex reason behind his architectural choices..."
target: “啊，年轻的工头……建筑师从不透露自己设计抉择背后的复杂原因……”

source: Mr. Hanson the architect stared at the building pridefully... and then he had a flashback of his own!
target: 建筑师汉森先生骄傲地望着大楼……然后，他也陷入了自己的回忆！

source: Mr. Hanson remembered playing Truth or Dare at the yearly architect pajama party years ago. "I pick truth!" said one architect.
target: 汉森先生想起几年前，在一年一度的建筑师睡衣派对上玩真心话大冒险。“我选真心话！”一位建筑师说。

source: "Okay," said another, "would you rather have sex with Frank Gehry, Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, or Antoni Gaudi?"
target: “好，”另一位说，“弗兰克·盖里、路德维希·密斯·凡·德·罗和安东尼·高迪，你更想跟谁上床？”

source: "Gaudi, obviously. Have you SEEN the way Mediterraneans fuck? It's joie de vivre in the streets, ravenous horndog in the sheets!"
target: “当然是高迪。你见过地中海人做爱有多猛吗？白天在街上热爱生活，晚上到床上如狼似虎！”

source: "My turn! I pick dare!" said Mr. Hanson.
target: “轮到我了！我选大冒险！”汉森先生说。

source: "Okay... I dare you to add a five-story-tall flamethrower in the next building you design!"
target: “好……我赌你不敢在下一栋设计的建筑里，装个五层楼高的火焰喷射器！”

source: WHOA! Is that skyscraper-mecha breathing fire now?
target: 哇！那台摩天大楼机甲开始喷火了？

source: I have no idea what's going on anymore!
target: 我已经完全搞不懂现在是什么情况了！

source: The skyscraper torches the kaiju, proving once again that Truth or Dare can save lives. You gain +N2 SOUL for giving buildings a chance to fight back!
target: 摩天大楼烧死了巨兽，再次证明真心话大冒险也能救命。给建筑们创造反击的机会，让你获得了 +N2 灵魂！

source: Evacuate the city
target: 疏散全城

source: You wisely decide today isn't the day to play the hero. Better to take the more practical approach and help people escape the kaiju. But there's a problem...
target: 你明智地决定，今天不当英雄。还是务实一点，帮市民逃离巨兽吧。不过出了个问题……
